pages.transcription:
8. June 1941 Hotel Wyndham Newyork
Dear Hannah, we just returned from Croton and I hurry to say you my
impressions as they are beyond my expectations. I found Eva grown-up,
sunburned, gay and happy; she is there loved with everybody, has with
Marion an excellent companion, takes care of the little children with real
passion and seriousness, loves very much her auntie Olga and the house. You
would have enjoyed to see her riding a little very tame pony which is now
for the whole summer in the house and most friendly with all the children.
We went in the car with Ron Wohl, the Berners and the little Robin who
knows Eva still from London; they all were surprised how beautiful the
place is now in summer time, overlooking the whole valley and very breezy
even in the hottest days. They will have soon tents there and allowed
as a special reward to sleep in them if they like — it is a kind of
life I wished to have had myself in my youth, free and amusing and
I feel it does Eva a lot of good. She has been always in company
of adults and learns now to deal with all the really important things
like housekeeping, care of little children, gardening and comes in con-
tact with life much better than with us who are only intellectuals (and
mostly disappointed ones). Lotte is really happy that all works so well as
she feels that you would enjoy to see your daughter so pleased with her
daily life, so healthy and so far from all the troubles and difficulties
of this damned time. It is also egoistically for us a great advantage that
she feels so thoroughly at home here because we can go with much better
confidence somewhere to a summer place - we have not yet decided where,
but I do not believe that we will leave before the first weeks of July as I
would prefer that Lotte continues her treatment as long as possible with
Dr. Shor. She feels much better but her activity, her „pep” as they say here
was a little hampered all these last months and I hope if we could find
a quiet place somewhere it would do her good; in summer Newyork is
like a furnace and even after Rio it would be a hard test to remain
here.
As to my material things I hear that some outstanding royalties
from Hungary will be paid directly to Paul Tabori in a few

and as soon as they arrive there, please inform me; it should be about
32 Pounds. As to Cassells I am convinced they will pay as soon as they will
be able to do so. We are now revising the translation of my book on
Brazil. The proofs will go to Cassels and I hope he can publish it next
year provided there is still enough paper available.
And now give my best wishes to Manfred for his exam and
do not forget to inform us by cable about the happy event which will
give him the well merited holidays - may: holy weeks, holy months -
in Bath. Altogether airmail is now much more rapid than before
and ~~though~~ {thanks to} that we feel you somewhat nearer to us. Kindest regards
to you all. Yours

Stefan Zweig

Dear Hanna & Manfred, We enjoyed the afternoon yesterday with Eva,
and I hope that the photos we took will come out well and give
you and Carmel some pleasure. Her vacations will begin earlier
than expected, practically already in a fortnight, and will last
until the middle of september. We are still uncertain when and where
to go for the summer, but I suppose we will have Eva with us
for a few days still here in Newyork. There are one or two little
things to be done about her teeth which the dentist could not fix
when she was here last owing to the holidays. - Our life continues
unchanged. Stefan is working at the autobiography, we are revising the
translation of the Brazil book, and last week we had a large cock-
tail party collecting all of Stefan's native friends, collegues and
acquaintances. It was nice, apparently so much so that nearly all
people remained not only for a cocktail but for more than two hours.
Twice a week I get my injections of dust and bacterias (separately) and
occasionally adrenaline in oil, and all this, together with the little
things one has always to attend to - this week for instance trying
to exchange the typewriters, getting summer shirts for Stefan, looking at a
house near Newyork, interviewing a prospective help, business talks,
having photostats made of several documents - keeps us busy.
I hope you are both well, that Manfred is not
working too hard and will soon get his degree and that you Hanna, have
nothing more to do with the dentist. We saw your last letter to Eva
which took only a week.
Love and kisses, Lotte
